title: API 570 Training in San Francisco: Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 570 exam prep for Bay Area piping inspectors: CML programmes after renewable conversions, traced lines and CUI, terminal manifolds.
h1: API 570 Training in the San Francisco Bay Area: Online Exam Prep for Refinery, Renewable Fuels and Terminal Piping Inspectors
html:
API 570 exam prep for piping inspectors from Richmond to Rodeo and Martinez

Piping takes a large share of the inspection hours at any Bay Area plant. A refinery or renewable fuels plant has far more line than vessels, and every circuit needs condition monitoring locations, corrosion rates, an interval and someone who can defend all three to an auditor. This page is for the inspectors and NDT technicians who read those lines, the pipefitters and welders who repair them, and the engineers who approve the plans, all preparing for the API 570 Piping Inspector examination.

There is no Atlantis classroom in the San Francisco Bay Area, and no Atlantis classroom stands anywhere in San Francisco, Oakland or the Contra Costa refinery towns. Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad; its API 570 course is studied online at your own pace, with an instructor who answers your questions. The American Petroleum Institute sets the eligibility rules, administers the examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification, and each candidate applies to API individually. Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider, and the course does not grant certification.

Where the piping is: units, conversions and terminal manifolds

Two crude refineries remain in the region. EIA's survey for January 2026 lists Chevron at Richmond, with catalytic cracking, gas oil hydrocracking, reforming and solvent deasphalting, and Martinez Refining Company, the former Shell plant now run by PBF Energy, with coking, catalytic cracking and hydrocracking. Each runs a dense network of circuits between those units, the crude and product tank farms and the docks. Valero's Benicia refinery appears in the same survey, but EIA reports that it has stopped refining.

The two converted plants are just as piping-heavy, and much of their pipe is new to its service. At Rodeo, Phillips 66 added pretreatment units, and the project description in Oil & Gas Journal said new piping would connect them to storage tanks and process units and that the marine terminal would receive renewable feedstocks instead of crude and gas oils. At Martinez Renewables, the Marathon and Neste joint venture, the plans described modifying existing hydroprocessing units while a crude unit, a gasoline hydrotreater, an alkylation unit and other refinery units were scheduled for removal, and the same description said feedstock arriving by rail would be moved onto barges at third-party terminals because the site cannot unload trains.

Outside the refinery fences, terminals add manifolds, dock lines and transfer piping. Kinder Morgan's Pacific operations brochure lists a Richmond products terminal with a ship dock, a five-lane truck rack and an 8 in. line to and from its Richmond station, and a separate Richmond chemical terminal handling chemicals, oilseeds, lubes and waxes. Sunoco LP lists a Selby terminal at Crockett with a single berth and rail service, and IMTT lists a Richmond terminal that handles renewable diesel, biofuels and specialty chemicals. Lines that leave these sites as pipelines, such as Kinder Morgan's SFPP system out of Richmond and Concord, come under pipeline safety rules rather than API 570, and where one regime hands over to the other is set by the regulations and the owner's records, not by the nearest flange.

When a circuit changes service: rates, CMLs and materials

A conversion breaks the one thing a piping inspector relies on most: corrosion history. A circuit that carried gas oil for decades and now carries pretreated vegetable oil, or the effluent from a renewable diesel reactor, has rates that describe a fluid it no longer sees. API 570 gives the inspector ways to estimate a probable rate for new piping or piping in changed service until readings in the new service exist, and because the Body of Knowledge makes the whole of API 570 subject to testing, candidates should know them alongside the long-term and short-term rate formulas.

In practice, Bay Area piping groups handling a conversion do three things. They re-baseline the condition monitoring locations, often adding CMLs at elbows, tees and reducers where the new fluid may attack the wall differently. They review materials: a 2023 Inspectioneering article on renewable conversions notes that fatty acid attack calls for molybdenum-bearing stainless grades such as 316 and 317L, and that chlorides, which can be high in used cooking oil, accelerate it. And they verify that the alloy actually installed is the alloy specified, which is the subject of API RP 578. The current API 570 Body of Knowledge says the whole of RP 578 is subject to testing, including methods of positive material identification and the records that go with them, so a candidate who has worked a conversion turnaround already knows some of the exam's favourite questions.

Worked example: a CML whose rate changed after a conversion

These readings are for practice and describe no real line. A CML on a carbon steel feed line read 0.344 in. thirteen years ago at baseline and 0.318 in. four years ago, the last reading in petroleum service. The line was then converted. It read 0.301 in. a year ago and 0.284 in. today. The owner's minimum required thickness, the greater of pressure design and structural minimum, is 0.180 in.

  • Long-term rate from baseline: (0.344 − 0.284) ÷ 13 = 0.0046 in. per year.
  • Rate across the converted service only: (0.318 − 0.284) ÷ 4 = 0.0085 in. per year.
  • Short-term rate from the last two readings: (0.301 − 0.284) ÷ 1 = 0.017 in. per year.
  • Remaining life at the short-term rate: (0.284 − 0.180) ÷ 0.017 = about 6.1 years, so the thickness interval is about 3.1 years, half the remaining life.
  • At the long-term rate the same arithmetic gives about 22.5 years of life, and the interval would simply default to the class maximum.

API 570 leaves the choice of rate to the inspector, working with a corrosion specialist, as the one that best reflects current conditions. Here the long-term rate averages nine years of gas oil service into the answer and hides the acceleration. A one-year base is short for ultrasonic readings, so a careful inspector confirms the short-term rate with repeat readings, more CMLs or a scan before trusting it, and in the meantime plans from the faster figure. Exam questions often give three readings and ask which rate to use; read the story around the numbers.

Steam tracing, heated feed lines and CUI on the Carquinez Strait

Some renewable feedstocks, animal fats among them, thicken as they cool, so feed lines and the tanks behind them are often heated and traced. Traced and insulated pipe is classic territory for corrosion under insulation: a leaking steam tracer, a torn jacket or water that tracks down a vertical run keeps the insulation wet, and the pipe underneath sits in the temperature band where corrosion under insulation is most aggressive. Insulated austenitic stainless steel adds the risk of chloride stress corrosion cracking from the outside surface, and chloride stress corrosion cracking is also on the API 570 list. The plants at Rodeo and Martinez and the terminal at Crockett sit on the water, with fog, marine air and winter rain doing the rest.

For the examination, know where API 570 and RP 574 direct CUI inspection: damaged jacketing, insulation terminations and penetrations, low points, steam tracer entries and exits, and lines in intermittent or cyclic service that spend time in the susceptible temperature range. Read the susceptible ranges and inspection extents in the editions on your effectivity sheet rather than memorising figures from an old study guide; the ranges and extents are the kind of detail that moves between editions.

Injection points and water washes in hydroprocessing effluent

Hydroprocessing units commonly inject wash water upstream of their reactor effluent coolers, and the renewable units around the bay have their own reasons to. The Inspectioneering article describes carbon dioxide corrosion where water condenses in a renewable unit's effluent train, and notes that where the feed carries significant nitrogen, ammonium chloride concerns still dominate. That is why water wash points, and the piping downstream of them, are watched closely in those units.

API 570 singles out injection points prone to accelerated or localized corrosion for closer attention than ordinary piping: they can be treated as separate inspection circuits and are examined more thoroughly at scheduled inspections, and the interval guidance for them is something to read in the edition on your effectivity sheet. Exam questions test the circuit limits, the CML placement and what to examine when the line is opened. Learn the rules from the code text and RP 574, and treat any worked circuit you see as practice in reading the clause rather than a figure to remember.

Dead legs and lines left in place

Idling and conversion leave pipe behind. At Benicia, where Valero began idling process units in February 2026, and among the Martinez units that the conversion plans slated for removal, branches and whole lines can sit isolated but not yet demolished. A branch that still connects to live pipe is a dead leg in the sense API 570 means, and the stagnant end can corrode much faster than the active line. Two mechanisms on the API 570 Body of Knowledge list make this worse: microbiologically influenced corrosion, which thrives in stagnant water such as hydrotest water left in a line, and galvanic corrosion where dissimilar metals meet. Mechanical fatigue, including vibration-induced fatigue at small-bore connections near pumps and compressors, is also on the list. An inspector's first question about any idle pipe is simple: is it out of service and positively isolated, or is it still part of the system?

Routes into API 570 for Bay Area workers

API's scale combines education with piping experience gained in the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency: one year of piping inspection with a bachelor's degree in engineering or technology, two years with a two-year degree or certificate, three with a high school diploma and five or more without formal education, the longer routes each including at least a year supervising or performing inspection. The API 570 certification requirements page has the full scale. Common starting points here:

  • Pipefitters and pipe welders from turnaround and maintenance contractors. Fabrication and repair count as piping experience; the year of inspection is what most need to add. The AWS CWI exam prep for the Bay Area page covers a parallel welding inspector route.
  • UT technicians who have taken CML readings through several turnarounds. The NDT training in the San Francisco Bay Area page covers the ASNT steps before API.
  • Process technicians who moved into inspection after operating units at a refinery or chemical plant.
  • Engineers in reliability, corrosion or inspection groups, including those who worked on the renewable conversions.

Studying API 570 on a Bay Area schedule

Many open-book questions on API 570 send you into B31.3, while the closed-book half leans on API 570 itself, RP 574 and RP 571. A sequence that works for many Bay Area candidates: read API 570 until the inspection, interval and repair sections are familiar, drill the calculations, then move to RP 574, RP 571, RP 577 and RP 578, and finish with B31.3, B16.5, Section V, Section IX and PCC-2. Practise finding things in the B31.3 PDF, because the open-book questions reward speed in locating the right table more than reading the whole code.

Because the course is self-paced, a turnaround does not cost you a missed session; you pause, keep a few practice questions going and pick up the reading afterwards. Send the instructor the questions your own circuits raise, such as a rate that does not make sense after a service change or a CML that refuses to agree with its neighbours. Prometric lists test centres in and around the Bay Area, so pick a centre and an appointment time that allow for bridge traffic. The API 570 training overview and the API 570 code summary are useful companions.

Sponsoring a piping inspection group

Refinery inspection departments, the renewable fuels plants, terminal operators and the contractors that staff Bay Area turnarounds can enrol several candidates together. Each studies at their own pace, so a pipefitter preparing slowly and an engineer moving quickly do not hold each other back. Fees are quoted on request. Check each candidate's experience record against API's rules before enrolling, because no course changes eligibility, and tell us when you enquire whether some of your group are aiming at API 510 or API 653 instead.

faq.q: Are the Kinder Morgan pipelines out of Richmond and Concord API 570 piping?
faq.a: No. Kinder Morgan's brochure describes lines from its Richmond, Amorco and Concord stations to Brisbane, the Bay Area airports, Sacramento, San Jose and Fresno, and lines like these are regulated as hazardous liquid pipelines, not as process piping under API 570. Terminal and plant piping inside the fence is commonly inspected to API 570. Where one regime ends and the other starts is fixed by the regulations and the owner's records, so ask before you assume.

faq.q: What happens to a CML programme when a line changes to renewable feed?
faq.a: The old corrosion rates stop describing the line. Inspectors usually re-baseline the condition monitoring locations, add CMLs where the new fluid may attack differently, check that any alloy upgrades are the materials specified, and use a probable rate until readings in the new service exist. API 570 sets out how to estimate that rate, and since the whole code is subject to testing, learn those methods for the exam.

faq.q: Does steam tracing make corrosion under insulation more likely?
faq.a: It can. A leaking tracer or a poorly sealed tracer entry wets the insulation, and heat keeps the pipe in the temperature range where corrosion under insulation is most aggressive. Heated renewable feed lines and the older traced lines at Bay Area refineries both need CUI inspection planned around tracer entries, terminations and low points. Check the susceptible ranges in the editions on your effectivity sheet.

faq.q: Is positive material identification on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Yes. The current Body of Knowledge says the whole of API RP 578, the material verification programme, is subject to testing, and it lists methods of performing positive material identification and the related record keeping. Candidates who have checked alloy spools during a conversion or turnaround have a head start, but learn the RP 578 terms and responsibilities exactly as written.

faq.q: Can a pipefitter from a Bay Area contractor qualify for API 570?
faq.a: Often, yes. Fabrication and repair of piping count as experience, and with a high school diploma API asks for three years of piping experience, including at least one year supervising or performing piping inspection, all gained in the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency. Most fitters need to add that year of inspection. API checks the experience you record on the application.

faq.q: Should I take API 570 or API 510 first at a Bay Area refinery?
faq.a: Take the one that matches your work. Most inspection hours at refineries and renewable fuels plants go on piping, so many inspectors start with API 570 and add API 510 later; vessel specialists do the reverse. The two codes share inspection concepts, RP 571, RP 577, Section V and Section IX, so the second exam is easier after the first.

faq.q: Where do Bay Area candidates sit the API 570 exam?
faq.a: In person at a Prometric test centre, once API accepts your application. Choose your centre from Prometric's list for the region when you book. The day is about 7.5 hours with a closed-book part and an open-book part where the codes are provided as PDFs on screen, and you may not bring your own books or notes.
